title: Garlic Roast Leg of Lamb with Potatoes
subtitle: a boneless leg rubbed with garlic, lemon and dried rosemary, roasted over golden potatoes
imageAlt: Sliced garlic roast leg of lamb, pink in the centre, with golden roast potatoes on a cream plate beside a navy napkin
servingsNote: Easter dinner for 6, or for two with plenty of leftovers

breakdown: Dried rosemary and oregano, salt, pepper

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen lamb needs 1–2 days in the fridge to thaw; take it out 45 minutes before roasting.
A thermometer is the only sure way: pull it at 60°C for medium-rare, it rises to 63°C as it rests.

steps.title: Rub
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Mash the garlic, lemon zest, 1 tbsp lemon juice, olive oil, dried rosemary, dried oregano, salt and pepper into a paste and rub it all over the lamb.

steps.title: Potatoes
steps.text: Toss the potatoes with the olive oil and salt in a roasting pan and set the lamb on top (or on a rack over them).

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast 15 minutes, then lower to 175°C (350°F) and roast 60–80 minutes more, stirring the potatoes once, until the thickest part reads 60°C (140°F) for medium-rare or 68°C (155°F) for medium.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Move the lamb to a board, tent with foil and rest 15 minutes; it rises to at least 63°C (145°F). Keep the potatoes warm in the turned-off oven.

steps.title: Gravy
steps.text: Spoon off most of the fat from the pan, set it over medium, whisk in the flour 1 minute, then the broth and the rest of the lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Carve
steps.text: Snip off the netting, slice thinly against the grain and serve with the potatoes and gravy.

fixIt.fix: Lower the oven to 160°C (325°F) and keep going; the thermometer decides.
Move the lamb out to rest and crank the oven to 220°C (425°F) for 10 minutes.
Return slices to the hot gravy for a minute, or roast to 71°C (160°F) next time.

saleTip: Lamb legs go on sale at No Frills the week before Easter; a frozen New Zealand leg is often cheapest.
swap: Bone-in leg (add about 20 minutes). Pork loin roast with the same rub, to 71°C (160°F).
leftovers: Lamb pitas with tzatziki, or shepherd's pie with the chopped meat.
doneness: Whole cuts of lamb to at least 63°C (145°F) after resting for medium-rare, 71°C (160°F) for medium (Health Canada).
source: Based on tested roast leg of lamb methods (Canadian Living, BBC Good Food): garlic-herb paste, a 220°C start then 175°C, pulled at 60°C and rested.
gear: Roasting pan (with a rack if you have one)
prepAhead: Rub the lamb the night before and keep covered in the fridge.
reheat: Slices covered with a splash of gravy at 160°C (325°F) for 10–15 minutes, or in the microwave, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Garlic, lemon, salt and pepper lamb over potatoes; no herbs or gravy.

stepNotes.4: Basic: skip the gravy; spoon the pan juices over.

fancy.note: A honey-garlic glaze for the last 15 minutes and a red wine gravy.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: brush the honey over the lamb for the last 15 minutes.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: add the wine with the broth and simmer 5 minutes.

plating: Fan the slices, pink side up.
Potatoes around, gravy in a jug.

why.0-1: Lots of garlic mellows and sweetens as it roasts.
why.0-0: Boneless is easy to carve and cooks evenly.

funFact: Lamb at Easter goes back to the Passover lamb; it's the traditional Easter roast across much of Europe.
drink: A Merlot or Pinot Noir, or sparkling water with lemon.
